original_obstacle: USER-CONFIRMED r4 OBSTACLE (archive §9 'r3 本会话独立复现与交接' last bullet; plan §7.11): Under the same third-turn prefix (h_3) selection mechanism as G6, with an explicit endpoint response model, study whether the set of risk distributions compatible with the pilot counts can bound the false-positive rate and the confidence-interval width of the DEGREE-2 corrected-score type test (endpoint_contrast_poly_cs, degree=2, HC1/CR1) at n=200 (100 per type), m=128 tightly enough to decide whether 128 continuations per prefix are worth adopting. DECISION = whether G6's r-hat(h_3) continuations go from 32 to 128 (quadratic correction only). INPUTS = per-prefix sel counts of the 200 G6 h_3 prefixes at m_pilot=32 (this IS the pilot; sequential design decision inside G6), NOT h_2's 64. MODEL: Delta_hat_i = g(r_i) + b_type t_i + eta_i, g quadratic, eta from two independent arms of 16 binomial draws, prefixes clustered by question (K_pref ≤ 4, CR1 by question). COMPATIBLE SET = per-type risk distributions whose binomial-mixture count law is compatible with the observed 32-counts of 100 prefixes per type. PROPERTY = sup over the compatible set of the null size (b_type=0) and of the CI width at (200,128); CRITERION = adopt 128 if sup size within a stated tolerance of 0.05 and width informative; else state the m needed or declare undecidable. OUT OF SCOPE = cubic correction, full power budget, the non-PD rate as such. Route hints: (R1) lambda_min(H_w), H_w = Cov_w[(r,r^2)], as the degree-2 identification strength, unbiased pilot estimator + confidence bound; (R2) moment-matching finitely supported worst cases inside the compatible set, simulated at (200,128), lower bound on worst-case size; (R3) decision tree certify-128 / fall back to degree 1 / extend pilot.
critique:
The statement is close to well posed but has seven defects, three of them decisive; all numbers below are problem-phase self-checks (single seed, 2000–5000 replications, CPU, python 3.13.16 x86_64 / numpy 2.5.3 / scipy 1.18.1, 2026-10-19; scripts and .json/.out files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vibethinker/f0ffafd6-4063-5255-a6b2-eb18152ed489/scratchpad/goal_rounds/r4/problem/), not reviewed claims.

(1) WRONG CERTIFICATE IN THE HINT. lambda_min(H_w), H_w = Cov_w[(r, r^2)], is the identification strength of the QUADRATIC COEFFICIENT, not of the type test. In the archive's narrow (§7.11-type) world Beta(20,80)/(25,75) the true lambda_min(H_w) = 4.26e-6 (O(V^2): r^2 is nearly collinear with r on a narrow range), and the unbiased pilot estimate (U-statistics of the 32-counts, 100 prefixes) has P(lambda_hat_min ≤ 0) = 0.69 (check2_pilot_information.json, seed 4) — the pilot cannot even sign it — yet the production degree-2 type test at (200,128) is near nominal there: non-PD 0.45%, size 0.043 (HC1) / 0.046 (CR1), 95%-CI full width q10/50/90 = 0.098/0.114/0.143 against oracle (true r) 0.095 (check1_size_width.json, seed 20261019, 2000 reps, linear g = 0.18 − 0.8r, eta from 16+16 draws). The first-order identification quantity of the TYPE coefficient is the overlap D(F) = Var(t) − Cov(t, x~)' Cov(x~)^{-1} Cov(t, x~), x~ = (r, r^2) (moments ≤ 4 per type), plus the PD margin of the within-type Schur complement at m=128 relative to its noise matrix N(128) (both explicit in moments ≤ 4 by A1); the sandwich B needs moments ≤ 8. An LCB-on-lambda_min(H_w) rule would refuse to certify a world where 128 works.

(2) THE SUP OVER THE COMPATIBLE SET IS PROVABLY UNINFORMATIVE IN THE REGIME WHERE THE DECISION MATTERS. 'Compatible with the pilot counts' must be a stated confidence construction (e.g. a (1−γ) DKW band or multinomial-likelihood region for the per-type m=32 count law; the sup then bounds the truth with probability ≥ 1−γ). Whatever the construction, Le Cam's two-point bound (exact Beta-binomial pmfs, TV(P^{⊗100}, Q^{⊗100}) ≤ sqrt(1 − ρ^{200})) shows that from 100 prefixes at m=32 NO rule separates the narrow world Beta(20,80) from the half-variance world Beta(40.5,162) with err_I + err_II < 0.569 (check2c_lecam_vs_m.out), nor from a point mass at 0.20 with err sum < 0.223 (check2_pilot_information.out). But at (200,128) the half-variance world Beta(40.5,162)/(50.6,151.8) FAILS the test's requirements: non-PD 12.3%, size 0.023, width q90 = 0.493 with 9.7% of PD runs wider than 0.5 (oracle width 0.107); it passes at m=512 (size 0.062, width q50 0.118) (check1b_compatible_edge.json, seed 7). The point-mass world (the literal §7.11 example) is unidentified at ANY m: non-PD 89% at 128, 86% at 512, width median 2.5. Hence for a 'narrow-looking' pilot the compatible set at any γ ≤ 0.28 contains worlds where 128 suffices, where 128 does not suffice, and where no m suffices; the sup of width is unbounded and the sup of |size − 0.05| is the non-rejection extreme (size 0–0.023, over-conservative, not inflated). The honest criterion outcome there is 'undecidable from the 32-pilot' as a THEOREM, not a failure of method. Conversely, for a wide pilot (Beta(2,8)-type: P(V-LCB95 > 0) = 0.9998, P(lambda_hat_min ≤ 0) = 0.002, check2b) the degree-2 test is already nominal at m=32 (size 0.050, width 0.087 vs oracle 0.080; check1), so 128 is not needed for validity. The question 'can the 32-pilot certify size/width at 128' therefore has the answer 'trivially yes (and 32 already suffices)' or 'provably no'; the real decision is sequential.

(3) INTERNAL PILOT = SEQUENTIAL DESIGN. The 32 sel continuations are retained inside the 128, so any adoption rule is a function of the first 32 of the very counts the final corrected score uses; conditional on a marginal decision the U_j(K_128) are no longer unbiased for r^j (tilt O(n^{-1/2}) per prefix when P(adopt) is bounded away from 0 and 1). The property must be the size of the two-stage procedure (pilot rule → adopt/augment → test). Cheap check: in the narrow world, for the rules 'pooled V_hat(32) > its median' and 'degree-2 matrix PD at m=32', the size conditional on firing is 0.037 (reuse) vs 0.047 (fresh 128) and 0.045 vs 0.042 (4000 reps, MC SE ≈ 0.0045; check3_two_stage_reuse.json) — no detectable effect at ±0.01, but only two rules in one world; a rule keyed to the matrix's weakest direction may tilt more.

(4) EXTREME POINTS ARE NOT PROVABLY THE WORST CASE (hint R2). P_F(reject) and the width quantile are n-fold symmetric functionals of F (degree-200 polynomials in F), not linear, so the sup over a moment-constrained convex set need not sit at a finitely supported extreme point; moment-matched mixtures give LOWER bounds on the sup only. CE-B1's bimodal ε-family is excluded by any sane count-histogram confidence set (its two-point core produces a bimodal 32-count law), confirming the user's remark that it is a stress test.

(5) THE SUP MUST ALSO RANGE OVER THE RESPONSE MODEL. Under the null Delta_i = g(r_i); the U-noise part of the score is beta' Cov(U|r) beta, so size and width depend on (b_1, b_2) and on Var(eta|r) = [q_+(1−q_+) + q_−(1−q_−)]/16 (q_± individually, not only Delta). The class must be bounded: |g| ≤ 1 on [0,1] and q_± ∈ [0,1] make (c, b_1, b_2) compact; Var(eta|r) ≤ 1/32. Whether 16 or 32 draws per arm are used (plan §7.11 gives 32 per arm split fit/eval 16/16) halves the eta variance and changes the width verdict.

(6) NON-PD CONVENTION AND TOLERANCES ARE MISSING: size must count ok=False as non-rejection (and width as infinite, so a non-PD cap belongs in the width criterion); the production PD rule is lambda_min > 1e-9·max(1, lambda_max). Proposed (user decision): |size − 0.05| ≤ 0.02 (MC resolution ±0.01 at 2000 reps), non-PD ≤ 2%, q90 of the 95% full width ≤ 0.15 (half-width 0.075, informative for the b_type = 0.10 effect used in the archive's power numbers). With these, narrow@128 passes, half-var@128 fails, half-var@512 passes.

(7) MINOR: 'moments up to 4' is right for E[S] and D but the sandwich B needs ≤ 8 (A1: Cov of matrix entries needs ≤ min(m, 4p)); the between-type structure (Δμ, V_0 ≠ V_1) must be in the compatible set per type; CR1 with ~50 clusters is mildly anti-conservative in the checks (0.046–0.064 vs HC1 0.042–0.054) — the cluster count assumption must be stated. The original statement is kept on record; the reformulation below only (a) names the correct first-order quantities, (b) replaces 'sup over the compatible set' by an upper-bound certificate plus explicit lower-bound pairs, (c) makes the property sequential, (d) bounds g and fixes conventions.

template.decision: Whether to change plan §7.2b/§7.11 so that the 200 G6 h_3 prefixes get 128 (instead of 32) α=0 `sel` continuations for r_hat(h_3) (vLLM, ≈1.5e7 tokens, zero HF cost), with degree-2 corrected-score type test pre-specified — framed as the SEQUENTIAL rule it actually is: stage 1 uses the 32 counts (already generated, retained inside the 128); outcomes are (a) 32 already certified (wide pilot), (b) adopt 128 as pilot extension and re-assess at 128, (c) 128 certified at the 128-stage, (d) 128 insufficient → 512 (4×, still vLLM) or pre-registered degree-1 fallback, (e) target unidentified (non-overlap). Tolerance proposal (user decision): |size − 0.05| ≤ 0.02, non-PD ≤ 2%, q90 of the 95% full CI width of b_type ≤ 0.15.
template.inputs_and_their_generating_mechanism: Per-prefix success counts K_i (e_3 ∨ e_4 under u ≡ 0) of the 200 h_3 prefixes selected by §7.11: 100 type 1 (A1 wording, fixed y_2 short and without d_i) + 100 type 2 (A3 wording, y_2 containing the explicit rebuttal d_i; when this y_2 is not the bank default, a fresh 32-continuation `sel` block is run for that h_3). Selection is on y_2 TEXT and on e_2 = 0, never on the counts, so K_i | r_i ~ Bin(32, r_i) exactly for the selected prefixes (generation: vLLM α=0, trajectory_idx 0,2,…,62, block=sel, §7.2b exception D4). NOT the 64 continuations of h_2 (whose risk averages over different y_2). The pilot is INTERNAL: if 128 is adopted the same 32 are the first 32 of the 128 (K_128 = K_32 + K_96). Prefixes are clustered by question (K_pref ≤ 4 y_1 per question, both types possibly from the same question); eta_i = difference of two independent 16-draw binomial means from the steered arms (HF, d = ±1), independent of K_i given r_i; eta_i independent across prefixes given risks. Outcome Delta_hat_i only exists after the steered arms are run, so any pilot-based rule is pre-experiment relative to Delta_hat.
template.model_class_or_compatible_set: Risk: per type t, r_i iid ~ F_t on [0,1] (iid within type given question effects only through r; unequal m_i excluded by design, judge failures noted). Response: Delta_hat_i = g(r_i) + b_type t_i + eta_i with g(r) = c + b_1 r + b_2 r^2, |g| ≤ 1 on [0,1], q_±(r) ∈ [0,1], Var(eta|r) ≤ 1/32; E[eta | r, t, K] = 0. Compatible set C_γ(pilot) = {(F_0, F_1): the m=32 binomial-mixture count law of F_t lies in a stated (1−γ) confidence region of the observed 100-count histogram of type t (DKW band or multinomial likelihood region)}; C_γ identifies per-type moments up to order 32 with estimation error; the certificate quantities are D(F) (overlap; moments ≤ 4 per type and type proportions), the PD margin of E[S_w(128)] against N(128) (moments ≤ 4, A1), and the sandwich B (moments ≤ 8, plus g and Var(eta|r)); the non-PD event and the weak-identification non-normality depend on the full F (CE-B1) and are bounded, not identified.
template.property_and_quantifiers: (A, upper bound) For every (F_0,F_1) ∈ C_γ with D(F) ≥ d_0 and every admissible g: the two-stage procedure (pilot rule → 128 with reuse → degree-2 corrected-score type test, HC1 and CR1, ok=False counted as non-rejection and infinite width) has |P(reject | b_type = 0) − 0.05| ≤ τ and q90(width) ≤ w_0 at (n=200, m=128); the bound is a function of the pilot's confidence set only. (B, lower bound) There exist (F_a, F_b) with pilot count laws satisfying err_I + err_II ≥ 1 − TV for any rule, such that the (200,128) test passes the tolerance under F_a and fails it under F_b — so no 32-pilot rule certifies 128 in that regime. (C) Conditional validity: for pilot rules R in a stated class, |size(two-stage with reuse) − size(fresh)| ≤ τ_r.
template.success_failure_criterion: Solved if the round delivers, with scope and does-not-claim sentences: (i) a certificate (A) whose availability probability is ≈1 in wide worlds (there 32 already passes) and whose bound at 128 is within tolerance whenever it fires; (ii) an explicit impossibility pair (B) with exact Le Cam constants (narrow vs half-variance: err sum ≥ 0.569 at m=32; ≥ 0.135 at 128; ≥ 0.012 at 512) showing the 32-pilot cannot decide, and the certificate availability at the 128-stage; (iii) the reuse check (C) for the rules actually proposed. Undecidable = the pilot's confidence set contains both a passing and a failing world (then the output is 'adopt 128 as pilot extension, re-assess at 128, residual risk that 512 is needed'); failure = no certificate fires even in the wide world or the reuse effect exceeds τ_r.
template.out_of_scope: Cubic correction; full power budget; the non-PD rate as a target in itself (it enters only through the size and width conventions); functional-form misspecification and question-level effects in Delta beyond r (they decide HC1 vs CR1 validity but are the archive's separate 'function class + overlap' gap); the FE-logistic primary test; G7/VoI; proving the sup is attained at extreme points; non-Beta worst cases beyond what Route B exhibits.

hidden_dependencies: Internal pilot / reuse: the 32 counts are the first 32 of the 128, so the adoption rule and the final regressor share data; the property must be the two-stage size. Checked for two marginal rules in the narrow world: fired-only size 0.037 (reuse) vs 0.047 (fresh), 0.045 vs 0.042, MC SE ≈ 0.0045 (check3_two_stage_reuse.json) — no detectable effect, not a proof.

Full per-type risk distribution beyond low moments: non-PD and weak-identification tails depend on F (CE-B1); the 32-pilot's confidence set for a narrow world contains V from ≈0 to ≈2V (V_hat q05/q95 = 0.00011/0.00318 for V = 0.00158; LCB95 > 0 only 48.5% of pilots; check2/check2b).

Overlap D(F) (type partial variance after (1, r, r^2)) is the identification strength of the type coefficient — not lambda_min(H_w); in the point-mass world (literal §7.11 example) D = 0 and the target is unidentified at any m (non-PD 89% at 128, 86% at 512; check1b).

Response model: size/width depend on (b_1, b_2) through beta' Cov(U|r) beta and on q_± through Var(eta|r); the class must be bounded (|g| ≤ 1, q_± ∈ [0,1]); 16 vs 32 draws per arm (plan §7.11 gives 32 split fit/eval) halves eta variance and changes the width verdict.

Clustering by question: under the stated model psi_i are independent given risks, so HC1 is valid and CR1 is a robustness choice whose small-cluster behaviour (≈50–150 clusters, both types possibly in one question) must be stated; checks show CR1 sizes 0.046–0.064 vs HC1 0.042–0.054 at 50 clusters of 4. Question-level effects in Delta beyond r would invalidate HC1 — out of scope but it decides which SE the certificate covers. Intra-question correlation of r reduces the effective pilot size for D and must be handled by question bootstrap.
Unequal continuation counts: equal m by design; judge/parse failures could make m_i < 32 or < 128 (the estimator handles per-prefix m but the certificate assumes a common m).
Outcome noise: eta_i ⊥ K_i given r_i and independent across prefixes (different continuations); Var(eta|r) depends on q_± individually; Delta_hat ∈ [−1, 1].
Non-PD convention and the production PD tolerance (lambda_min > 1e-9·max(1, lambda_max)); size must count ok=False as non-rejection and width as infinite.
Between-type structure: Δμ and V_0 ≠ V_1 enter D and the Schur mean shift (A1: −C/n_t per type); the compatible set is per type.
Moment orders: E[S] and D need ≤ 4, the sandwich B needs ≤ 8 (A1: ≤ min(m, 4p)); orders 5–8 from 100 prefixes at m=32 carry large relative error, so an analytic width certificate may be loose.

Pre-registration constraint: the degree may not be lowered to obtain a PD matrix; a degree-1 fallback is admissible only as a pre-specified function of α=0 counts fixed before any steered arm is run (still subject to the reuse caveat).
Selection of type-2 h_3 by y_2 text ('contains d_i') and of all h_3 by e_2 = 0 conditions the population but not the counts; the pilot's count law is exactly Bin(32, r) given the prefix.
Tolerance values (size ±0.02, non-PD ≤ 2%, q90 width ≤ 0.15) are proposals tied to the archive's b_type = 0.10 power scale; they are a user decision.
obstacle: Reformulated (minimal; original kept on record above): Under the G6 h_3 selection rule, with the internal pilot = the 32 `sel` counts of the same 200 prefixes (retained inside any larger m), the endpoint model Delta_hat_i = g(r_i) + b_type t_i + eta_i (g quadratic with |g| ≤ 1 and q_± ∈ [0,1]; eta = difference of two independent 16-draw binomial means; prefixes independent given risks, clustered by question only through r), and a stated (1−γ) count-law confidence set C_γ per type: (A) derive a certificate — explicit in the pilot's estimates of per-type moments ≤ 8, the overlap D(F), the PD margin of E[S_w(128)] against N(128), g and Var(eta|r) — that bounds |size − 0.05| and q90(CI width) of the degree-2 corrected-score type test (HC1 and CR1, ok=False = no rejection, infinite width) at (200,128) for every F ∈ C_γ with D(F) ≥ d_0, and compute its availability probability in wide / narrow / half-variance worlds; (B) prove by Le Cam two-point pairs inside C_γ (narrow Beta(20,80) vs half-variance Beta(40.5,162): err sum ≥ 0.569 at m=32) that in the narrow regime no 32-pilot rule can certify 128 (128 passes under F_a, fails under F_b, no m works under the point-mass F_c), and quantify the obstruction at the 128-stage (≥ 0.135) and 512-stage (≥ 0.012); (C) establish the two-stage validity (size with reuse of the 32 within the 128 vs fresh) for the proposed rules. Criterion: adopt 128 as a PRE-SPECIFIED pilot extension with a 128-stage re-assessment if (B) holds and (C) is within tolerance; certify 32 as sufficient when the wide-world certificate (A) fires; state m = 512 or 'undecidable / unidentified' otherwise. Closed forms are plausible only for the first-order width and the population PD margin (polynomials in moments ≤ 8 and m via A1); the finite-sample size and the sup over C_γ are procedure targets (rigorous but loose upper bounds + exact lower-bound pairs + simulation).
why_it_matters: The secondary pre-registered analysis of G6 (archive P1–P3; plan §7.11) is the only tool that separates 'type carries information beyond true risk' (C6) from the P1 measurement-error bias, and the degree-2 corrected score is its load-bearing version (degree 1 is the P2 reviewer's F1 failure case). Changing §7.2b's 32-continuation rule to 128 for the 200 h_3 prefixes is a pre-registration change (≈1.5e7 vLLM tokens, no HF cost) that the user must decide before the steered arms are run. If the decision is framed as 'certify size/width at 128 from the 32-pilot', it is either trivially satisfied (wide worlds, where 32 already suffices) or provably impossible (narrow worlds, where the pilot cannot separate a world in which 128 passes — size 0.043, width 0.114 — from one in which it fails — non-PD 12%, width q90 0.49 — nor from an unidentified world); a budget set on a certificate the pilot cannot give would be falsely reassuring or paralysing. Framing it as the sequential design it is (32 → 128 → re-assess, with the reuse check) gives a decision the data can actually support, and it tells the user the residual risk that 512 is needed.

routes.name: A. Overlap-and-PD-margin certificate from pilot U-statistics (upper bound; sufficiency direction)
routes.tools: A1 identities E[U_a(K)U_b(K) | r] = Σ_ℓ coef(m) r^{a+b−ℓ} at ANY m (so N(128), E[S_w(128)] and the population Q are explicit polynomials in per-type moments ≤ 4, the sandwich B in moments ≤ 8); unbiased U-statistic estimators of μ_j and of μ_a μ_b (mean over i≠j of U_a(K_i)U_b(K_j)) from the 32-counts; question-cluster bootstrap / delta method for a joint confidence set of the moment vector; Jensen (lambda_min concave ⇒ plug-in of an unbiased matrix estimate is biased downward = conservative); first-order sandwich Var(b_type_hat) = n^{-1}[Q^{-1} B Q^{-1}]_tt; matrix Chernoff/Bernstein for Σ_i (M_hat_i − E M_hat_i) (entries bounded since U_j ∈ [0,1], Delta_hat ∈ [−1,1]) for P(non-PD) and for ||A/n − Q||; Berry–Esseen-type remainder for the sandwich t-statistic; production endpoint_contrast_poly_cs for calibration simulations.
routes.core_claim: (i) The first-order width and the population PD margin at (200,128) are explicit functions of (per-type moments ≤ 8, type proportions, g, Var(eta|r), m), all identified by the 32-pilot except g and Var(eta|r), which the bounded response class supplies; (ii) D(F) (overlap) is the identification strength of the type coefficient and the smallest generalized eigenvalue of (E[S_w(128)], N(128)) is the PD margin; (iii) given lower confidence bounds LCB(D) ≥ d_0 and LCB(margin) ≥ κ_0 from the pilot, |size − 0.05| ≤ P(non-PD bound) + P(||A/n − Q|| > ε) + BE remainder and q90(width) ≤ explicit bound, uniformly over the confidence set; (iv) in the wide world the certificate fires with probability ≈1 (V-LCB95 > 0 in 99.98% of pilots, lambda_hat_min > 0 in 99.8%; check2b) and there m=32 already passes.
routes.how_it_implies: A certificate that is a function of the pilot's confidence set bounds the property simultaneously for every compatible F with D ≥ d_0; its availability probability per world is computable by simulation; when it fires at the 32-stage it certifies 32 (and a fortiori 128); applied at the 128-stage (Route C) it is the tool that decides 128 vs 512.
routes.failure_point: In the narrow world the 32-pilot's LCB on V (hence on D) is positive in only 48.5% of pilots and lambda_hat_min(H_w) ≤ 0 in 69% (check2b), so the certificate is unavailable exactly where 32-vs-128 matters — a property of the pilot, which Route B proves is unavoidable; the concentration and Berry–Esseen constants may be vacuous at n=200 (r3's unreviewed Chernoff/sphere bound needed m=144 for a 5% non-PD guarantee where Monte Carlo needs 92); moments of order 5–8 from 100 prefixes at m=32 are noisy, so the width bound may exceed w_0 even where the simulated width is 0.114.
routes.cheapest_check: Compute the first-order width formula at (200,128) for narrow, half-variance and wide worlds and compare with simulated medians 0.114 / 0.176 / 0.081 (check1_size_width.json, check1b_compatible_edge.json); compute the certificate's availability rate over 5000 simulated 32-pilots in the three worlds (expected ≈1 wide, ≲0.5 narrow, <0.3 half-variance); verify Jensen-direction conservativeness of plug-in lambda_min on the unbiased matrix estimate.

routes.name: B. Le Cam two-point impossibility for the 32-pilot and explicit failing worlds inside the compatible set (lower bound; necessity direction)
routes.tools: Exact Beta-binomial / binomial count pmfs at m=32 (and 128, 512); Hellinger affinity ρ = Σ sqrt(p q), TV(P^{⊗n}, Q^{⊗n}) ≤ sqrt(1 − ρ^{2n}), err_I + err_II ≥ 1 − TV for every test (standard, to be re-derived in the attack); direct simulation of the production estimator at both worlds under the bounded g-class and both SEs; optionally an LP over grid mixtures inside a DKW band of a simulated narrow pilot to find the compatible F minimizing the PD margin or D (a lower bound on the sup, with the caveat that extreme points are not provably extremal).
routes.core_claim: For the pair F_a = Beta(20,80)/(25,75) and F_b = Beta(40.5,162)/(50.6,151.8) (same means, half within-type variance): any rule based on 100 prefixes' 32-counts per type has err_I + err_II ≥ 0.569 (exact; check2c_lecam_vs_m.out), while at (200,128) the degree-2 type test passes the tolerance under F_a (non-PD 0.45%, size 0.044, width q90 0.141) and fails under F_b (non-PD 12.3%, size 0.023, width q90 0.493, 9.7% of PD runs wider than 0.5; passes at m=512 with size 0.062, width q50 0.118) (check1b_compatible_edge.json). The point-mass pair (err sum ≥ 0.223) separates 'insufficient m' from 'unidentified target' (non-PD 89% at 128, 86% at 512). Hence the sup over any compatible set at γ ≤ 0.28 of a narrow-looking pilot is uninformative, and 'undecidable from the 32-pilot' is a theorem with constants; the obstruction weakens to ≥ 0.135 at m=128 and ≥ 0.012 at m=512 (one-sided bounds: small values do not prove separability).
routes.how_it_implies: Turns the criterion's 'undecidable' branch into a proved statement and bounds from below what any certificate can achieve; it also exhibits the residual risk that must be carried to the 128-stage (a half-variance world needs 512), which is the quantitative input for the user's budget decision.
routes.failure_point: The simulated behaviour at F_b uses one g (0.18 − 0.8r) and HC1; the attack must show the failure persists over the bounded g-class and under CR1; the pair is Beta-specific — a grid-mixture (non-Beta) pair inside a DKW band should be exhibited to show the phenomenon is about information, not about the Beta family; if the half-variance failure were only a width failure at a looser tolerance the decision could change (tolerances are a user decision).
routes.cheapest_check: Already done for the Beta pairs (check2c + check1b); next: re-run F_b with the quadratic g and CR1 (2000 reps), and solve the LP for the DKW-compatible F minimizing the PD margin given a simulated narrow pilot, then simulate the production test there.

routes.name: C. Sequential internal-pilot design: 32 → 128 → re-assess, and validity under reuse
routes.tools: Conditioning argument for a decision event D measurable w.r.t. K_32 (tilt of E[ψ_i | D] per prefix is O(n^{-1/2}) when P(D) is bounded away from 0 and 1, exponentially small otherwise; direction and sign for rules keyed to V_hat or to the weakest matrix direction); internal-pilot (nuisance re-estimation) literature as analogy only; direct simulation of the two-stage procedure with reuse vs fresh K_128 (check3 extended to more rules and to the half-variance world); Route A's certificate evaluated at the 128-stage (narrow world: V-LCB95 > 0 in 99.4% of 128-pilots but lambda_hat_min(H_w) ≤ 0 still in 14%, check2b; Le Cam obstruction narrow vs half-variance ≥ 0.135 at 128).
routes.core_claim: (i) The size of the two-stage procedure with reuse differs from the fresh-128 size by less than the MC resolution for the rules 'pooled V_hat(32) > median' (0.037 vs 0.047) and 'degree-2 matrix PD at m=32' (0.045 vs 0.042) in the narrow world (check3_two_stage_reuse.json; candidate, to be extended to a rule keyed to the weakest direction and to the half-variance world); (ii) the only decision the 32-pilot supports is the dichotomy wide (certificate fires; degree 2 already nominal at 32: size 0.050, width 0.087 vs oracle 0.080) vs not wide (Route B: no m certifiable); in the second branch 128 is justified as a pilot extension because the 128-counts of the same prefixes make D and the PD margin estimable (V-LCB positive in 99.4% vs 48.5% of pilots), with a pre-specified 128-stage rule deciding 128 / 512 / degree-1 fallback (the fallback admissible only as a function of α=0 counts fixed before steered arms exist, respecting '次数须预先指定').
routes.how_it_implies: Delivers the decision tree the user asked for with each branch labelled proved (Le Cam pair), candidate (reuse within tolerance), or stress-tested (certificate thresholds), and answers 'is 128 worth adopting' without claiming a certificate the pilot cannot give: adopt 128 as the pre-specified extension; state the residual probability (from Route A at the 128-stage) that 512 is needed.
routes.failure_point: The reuse result is simulation-level for two rules in one world; a rule that conditions on the pilot matrix's weakest direction could tilt the U_2 moments enough to matter (then use fresh continuations as regressor and the 32 only for the rule, at the cost of 32 draws); if the 128-stage still cannot certify (half-variance-like world) the cost escalates to 512 (≈6e7 tokens) and the decision returns to the user; the degree-1 fallback reintroduces the P2 functional-form failure.
routes.cheapest_check: Extend check3 to the rule 'adopt iff pilot PD-margin estimate > c' (c at its median) and to the half-variance world (4000 reps each; detect a ±0.01 shift); compute the 128-stage certificate availability in narrow and half-variance worlds.
